content.title: About
content.content: Canned grapefruit consists of sliced wedges or halves of grapefruit packed in glass or metal jars with syrup or its own juice. The canning process preserves most of the fruit's flavor and nutrients while providing a long shelf life without refrigeration.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Grapefruit was first cultivated in the early 19th century in the Caribbean as a hybrid of pomelo and sweet orange.
Canning retains a high amount of vitamin C, although it is slightly lower than in fresh fruit.
The syrup used in jars often contains a modest amount of sugar to balance the natural bitterness of grapefruit.
Canned grapefruit is frequently used in salads, desserts, and seafood dishes.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system, aids collagen synthesis, and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports normal heart function.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Canned grapefruit is low in calories, making it a suitable choice for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and contributes to a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Flavonoids
items.content: Flavonoids such as naringenin have anti‑inflammatory and antioxidant properties.

items.title: Bitterness
items.content: Some people may find canned grapefruit overly bitter, especially if the fruit was not fully ripe before processing.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Grapefruit can affect the metabolism of certain medications, potentially increasing their effects.

items.title: Added sugar in syrup
items.content: The syrup may add extra sugar, which should be considered by individuals with diabetes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned grapefruit can be eaten straight from the jar, added to fruit salads, yogurts, smoothies, used in desserts, or served as a side with seafood. Drain excess syrup before serving if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place. Once opened, keep the jar refrigerated in its original container and consume within 5–7 days.
